x: Emery with us again and hope to see more of him, and L. Demmon, one of our latest acquisitions, will undoubtedly prove a useful walker with more training.
The 2 miles walk handicap was won by Eric Hall, with George Oliver second and L. Demmon third, and the back-markers did not seem to have much chance of catching their field.
The result showed a decided improvement in all our walkers and hopes of greater successes in the future. In addition Len Demmon was third in the individual handicap.
Nevertheless we finished 4th in the scratch race with George Checkley 13th, Erich Hall 22nd, George Beecham 25th, and Len Demmon 26th. The "A" Team were also 4th in the handicap.
…er the last 100 yards by an enthusiastic band of runners returning from the common. Bob Phillips was 4 secs behind with Len Demmon 3rd in 59.23.…

Our Middlesex members, racing as Cadogan A.C. were led home by Hugh McGreechan in 10th position (82.37), with George Checkley 12th (84.02), Len Demmon 14th (84.46) and Harry Shields 27th (90.19). making a score of 62 points, only one point out for a place, the Poly being 3rd with 61 points.
To Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday, Len Demmon and Billie True and the ladies who came along to give their help and support ,we say thank you very much.
2 mile walk · 1. S.James; 2. G.Checkley; 3.L.Demmon · 15m. 21.s
Belgrave were well represented in the Marches with five members in the Police team (Bob Readman, Syd Spencer, Len Demmon, Charlie McLennan and Don Fotheringham) and myself in the R.W.A.

George Checkley was 2nd in the 5 miles, Syd James 2nd in 4 miles, George Beecham 5th in 4 miles, up and coming Ray Middleton 4th and George Oliver 6th in the 3 miles and Len Demmon 4th in the 2 miles.

Looked after and urged on by a grand bunch of supporters - Bob Newson, Len Demmon, Billy True - they consolidated their positions and the scoring four of Mac, Norman, Bernard and Harry were ably backed up by George Checkley, George Beecham, Joe Wilson, Gordon Doubleday and Fred Rolfe, finishing posi…
Syd James walked well within himself to be the first man home in 47m. 41s. with R.E. Green 2nd and Len Demmon 3rd in 49m. 23s.
Len Demmon was 2nd with George Beecham 3rd. There were 13 starters and our handicapper, Bill True, with a time of 62m.57s (all.7.15) was second in the handicap with Pot Hunter Harry Shields 3rd.

Bob Newson has shown considerably improvement, so also has "The Demon King", I mean Len Demmon. With these three we have the basis of a fine "Garnet" Cup team and as I expect this Championship will be over by the time you receive this issue, I hope we shall have the cup back in our possession by that time.
Len Demmon was our first man to finish in the "A" section which was won by Coleman of Highgate who covered 8 miles, 76 yards, an excellent performance.

We opened our winter season as usual with a five miles handicap and match with our Police friends. 40 competitors started and Eric Hall, carrying on his summer form, won a good race in 37m. 17s. with Hugh McGreechan 2nd and Len Demmon 3rd.

We had a good entry of 34 individuals but unfortunately we lost Eric Hall, Syd James, Norman Guilmant and Bill Ferguson and our first man home was Hugh McGreechan in 31st position. Bob Newson 55th, Gerry Warr [illegible]2nd and Len Demmon 63, made up our scoring four who finished 9th in the team race with 201 points.
Our lads certainly showed up better in this race, always among the leading bunch were Syd James, 11th, Eric Hall 16th, George Checkley 18th and Len Demmon 23rd.

Not disheartened, the other lads walked exceptionally well and with Eric Hall 11th, George Checkley 16th, Len Demmon 18th and Bob Newson 28th we totalled 68 points to finish 3rd to Woodford Green 21 points, with Met.
A nice exhibition of packing by Len Demmon 16th, Bob Newson 18th and George Checkley 19th, with a tolal of 53 points, once again secured us 3rd place.

Bob Newson was a good second in 57m. 10secs. with Len Demmon third, as last year in exactly 60mins. One or two of the newer members walked exceedingly well and George Place took the Novice's prize which was donated by Eric Hall.

Len Demmon, 14th made up the team. Bob Newson capably carried out the duties of Captain in the absence of Harry Shields and taking everything into consideration, the "Cads" left the Polytechnic very pleased with themselves.
Beecham 36th, L.Demmon 41st, B.

Congratulations to George Checkley on taking third place in both the Metropolitan and the National Police 10 miles Championships. Also to Hugh McGreechan and Len Demmon who finished 4th and 5th in the Police "National".

Mac was 5th in 2.37.29 and Len Demmon 10th in 2.44.45. In the team race, three to score, we tied with Woodford Green at 19 points each, but as their third man was 9th, they took the first team awards.
Len Demmon trailed the Captain home in 3.13.13 with Bob Readman and Bill True just behind, followed by Cyril Yescombe continuing to show improvement.

At the moment most of our distance men have a Middlesex qualification and our team consisted of George, Bob Newson, Hugh McGreechan, Len Demmon, Bob Readman, Fred Rolfe and Cyril Yescombe, and of course Harry Shields.

Norman was well up for the Kilos with Bob walking well under control and Harry doing the same. Len Demmon, off night work and Cyril Yescombe were further back. Pace began to tell and positions changed.

Eric Hall walked an excellent race in the 2 miles to finish 2nd to R, Goodall in 15 mins. with Ted Smith 3rd in 15.18. George Beecham 8th and H.McGreechan 10th were our scorers in the 5 miles, George Oliver 10th in the 4 miles and R, Newson 6th and L.

Len Demmon, who looks like being charged with desertion from the Police, showed that he is getting back to form by finishing 3rd. Stan's time of 56.37, although only just outside the Club record, was achieved right out on his own, and may conceivably have been much faster had it been an open field.
8. · L. Demmon · 87.15

Ted Smith was not far behind with Len Demmon and Terry Clark moving up to complete the scoring four. At 3 miles the lads were holding their own and even at this stage it looked as though the team race was in the bag.
Syd James and Hugh McGreechan finished together in 1h. 44m. and Len Demmon and Trevor Luck certainly walked well. Harry Shields, with an allowance of 12 minutes, won the handicap.

The feature of the day was that Len Demmon, known to all as "Last minute Len" actually arrive haf an hour before the train was due to go. This was too much for the rest of the lads who promptly had a whip round and bought him a watch.
